newsitem.title: USA: CalEnergy secures financing for NYSEG deal.
newsitem.headline: CalEnergy secures financing for NYSEG deal.

text.p: CalEnergy Co said Wednesday it secured $1.9 billion in financing for its proposed takeover of New York State Electric and Gas Corp for $27.50 a share.
The company said it and its wholly-owned subsidiary CE Electric Inc signed fully-underwritten binding financing commitment agreements with Credit Suisse First Boston and Lehman Brothers.

CalEnergy said the agreements include new and amended revolving credit facilities totaling $400 million; a possible CalEnergy bridge financing facility of up to $500 million; and up to $1.0 billion in CE Electric credit facilities, made up of a $650 million five-year term loan and a $350 million five-year revolving credit facility.
The company also said it intends to offer up to $550 milion in debt and equity securities promptly, in which case it would not use the bridge financing facility.
CalEnergy said Tuesday it filed a shelf registration statement with the Securities and Exchange Commission for offerings of up to $1.5 billion.
CalEnergy launched a hostile tender offer for 9.9 percent of the New York utility's shares for $24.50 a share July 15. It also said it intended to buy the rest of the utility for $27.50 a share.
New York State Electric and Gas rejected the tender offer and the $27.50-a-share offer for the rest of the company, which values the utility at $1.9 billion, July 30.

CalEnergy's chief executive David Sokol said in a statement the financing provides the company "with all the financing flexibility necessary to complete the acquisition of the (utility's) shares on the terms we have previously proposed."
CalEnergy's tender offer for 9.9 percent of the utility's shares is scheduled to expire August 14.
Sokol said CalEnergy would "proceed in a determined fashion" to complete the acquisition and hoped to start merger negotiations with the utility's management.
CalEnergy's stock rose two to 39-5/8 Wednesday. New York State Electric and Gas shares hit a new 52-week high of 25-9/16, and traded at 25-1/2, up 1/2, in the early afternoon.
